caption: The image shows a decorative ceramic plate with intricate patterns and illustrations in shades of dark and light gray, giving it a monochrome appearance. The border of the plate is adorned with floral and scroll motifs, as well as two framed cartouches. The upper cartouche bears the inscription "AMERICA INDEPENDENT 1776" and the lower cartouche says "WASHINGTON BORN 1732 DIED 1799." On either side of the plate, smaller cartouches enclose detailed designs, one showing a building structure and the other unclear. The center of the plate features a scene displaying people in colonial-era clothing landing on a rocky shore with a rowboat, while a sailing ship is visible offshore to the left. The people appear to be disembarking, with some carrying muskets or tools, and the rocky landscape is rendered with dark and light contrasts. Above the central scene are the words "THE LANDING OF THE PILGRIMS," and on the right, below the horizon line, the names "Carver - Bradford, Winslow - Brewster & Standish" are inscribed. The overall composition and color are uniform in grayscale, emphasizing linework and contrast in the imagery and ornamental border.
title: Plate - "Landing of the Pilgrims"
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
